markets: US-based early-stage company; no verified product sales or international plans.
rationale: Early-stage consumer robotics firm with little brand awareness; F1 could give technology credibility but marketing is unproven.

name: Taktile
desc: Taktile sells an AI-powered decision platform that helps banks, lenders, fintechs and insurers automate credit and risk decisions.
markets: Customers in the US and Europe; US headquarters in New York with roots in Berlin.
rationale: Fintech software vendor to banks and lenders; financial brands such as Visa and Mastercard sponsor F1, giving B2B hospitality value.

name: Today AI
desc: Today AI offers an AI assistant that connects to a user's phone.
markets: Shanghai-based early-stage company; international availability and customers are not verified.
rationale: Early-stage consumer AI product with unverified reach and no known marketing activity; limited F1 partnership fit.

name: Twelve Labs
desc: Twelve Labs develops video understanding foundation models, Marengo and Pegasus, that let users search, analyse and generate text from video.
markets: Sold to developers and enterprises online; regional operations beyond the US are not confirmed.
rationale: Video AI relevant to sports and media content; F1 media and broadcast archives offer a technology tie-in.

name: Vecna Robotics
desc: Vecna Robotics makes autonomous mobile robots for warehouses, including pallet-moving tuggers and pallet jacks, plus fleet management software.
markets: Customers are US warehouses and distribution operators; no verified international operations.
rationale: Warehouse automation supplier with industrial buyers; F1 logistics hospitality is possible, but the brand is small and US-centred.

name: Vendasta
desc: Vendasta provides a white-label AI-powered customer acquisition and engagement platform for agencies and resellers serving local small businesses.
markets: Resellers and agencies in Canada, the US, Europe and Australia serve local businesses with its platform.
rationale: Software sold through agencies to small businesses; F1 offers partner hospitality, though marketing budget and consumer brand are limited.

name: Warp Sciences
desc: Warp Sciences is a life sciences infrastructure company, with products and customers not described in the available data.
markets: Based in South San Francisco; customers, products and international activity are not verified.
rationale: Little verified information on this company, its products or customers; any F1 partnership fit is purely speculative.

name: Aimia
desc: Aimia is a Canadian holding company that invests in businesses; it sold the Aeroplan loyalty programme in 2018.
markets: Toronto-based holding company with stakes in businesses such as Bozzetto and Mon Ethos.
rationale: Financial holding company with little consumer marketing today and no operating brand to promote; sponsorship is unlikely.
changed: Sold Aeroplan to Air Canada in 2018

name: Amity Corporation
desc: Amity Corporation is described by Crunchbase as a technology holding and investment company.
markets: Based in London; holdings, ownership and international activity are not verified.
rationale: Unrecognised holding company with unverified activity and holdings; any F1 partnership fit is purely speculative at this stage.

name: Arcee AI
desc: Arcee AI develops open-weight language models and tools for building and deploying them, selling to enterprises.
markets: US-based enterprise AI developer; international customers and operations are not verified.
rationale: Small AI model developer with enterprise buyers; AI sponsors such as Cohere exist in F1, but Arcee has little marketing profile.

name: BrightInsight
desc: BrightInsight provides a regulated digital health platform that pharma and medtech companies use to run connected drug and device programmes.
markets: Pharma and medtech customers; part of Flex; regional spread not confirmed.
rationale: B2B digital health platform inside a larger manufacturer; no consumer brand, so F1 fit is weak.

name: CAST AI
desc: CAST AI offers a Kubernetes automation platform that cuts cloud costs by optimising clusters across AWS, Google Cloud and Azure.
markets: Software and cloud-native customers worldwide; large engineering team in Lithuania alongside its Miami base.
rationale: Cloud cost software for technology firms; sector peers such as AWS and Dynatrace sponsor F1, giving technology showcase value.

name: Censys
desc: Censys provides internet intelligence and attack surface management software built on a search engine for internet-connected devices.
markets: Enterprise and government customers, mainly in the US; international operations not confirmed.
rationale: Cybersecurity vendor with enterprise buyers; sector rivals such as CrowdStrike and Zscaler sponsor F1, though Censys is small.

name: Code Metal
desc: Code Metal provides a platform for translating and verifying code for embedded systems and hardware, used in defence and aerospace.
markets: Customers are defence and aerospace firms, mainly US-based; no verified international operations.
rationale: Embedded engineering software for defence and aerospace; limited marketing and a defence customer base make F1 fit weak.

name: DataCanvas
desc: DataCanvas provides AI infrastructure and foundation software for machine learning, AI computing and data analytics to Chinese enterprises and institutions.
markets: Customers are enterprises and institutions in China; no verified international operations.
rationale: Chinese AI infrastructure vendor with domestic focus; F1 fit is limited to a technology showcase.

name: Gloo
desc: Gloo sells software and AI tools to churches, faith organisations and ministries for member engagement, communications and analytics.
markets: Customers are US churches and faith-based non-profits; no verified international operations.
rationale: Niche faith-sector software with a US audience that rarely overlaps F1; weak fit.

name: Granola
desc: Granola is an AI notepad for meetings that transcribes calls on the device and turns notes into summaries.
markets: Used by professionals and companies, sold online; operating regions beyond the UK and US are not confirmed.
rationale: Prosumer app popular with start-ups and investors; F1 offers brand awareness among professionals, similar to productivity sponsors such as Atlassian.

name: HavocAI
desc: HavocAI builds autonomous surface vessels and AI software for unmanned boats used by the US military and allies.
markets: Sells to the US military and allied governments; defence-only customer base.
rationale: Defence supplier selling uncrewed military vessels; weapons-related positioning makes a mainstream F1 sponsorship very unlikely.

name: interos.ai
desc: interos.ai uses AI to map and monitor suppliers and detect risks across supply chains for large corporations and government agencies.
markets: Corporate and government customers mainly in the US; international customers are not confirmed.
rationale: Enterprise supply chain software with B2B and government buyers; F1 logistics hospitality is plausible but brand is little known.

name: Kaiko
desc: Kaiko provides crypto market data, analytics and benchmark indices for digital assets to exchanges, asset managers, banks and hedge funds.
markets: Clients are exchanges, banks and funds in Europe, the US and Asia; Paris headquarters.
rationale: Crypto data provider serving exchanges that already sponsor F1 such as Coinbase and Kraken; B2B hospitality value, modest brand.

name: LiveKit
desc: LiveKit develops open-source real-time audio and video infrastructure that developers use to build voice and video AI applications.
markets: Developers worldwide use it; it powers OpenAI's ChatGPT voice mode; operating regions beyond the US not confirmed.
rationale: Developer platform with high AI profile; F1 technology partnerships such as with Anthropic and Cohere suggest a plausible showcase.

name: Mytra
desc: Mytra builds a software-defined warehouse storage and retrieval system using robots on a modular steel grid.
markets: Customers are US warehouses and distribution operators; no verified international operations.
rationale: Early-stage warehouse automation firm with industrial buyers and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Netweb Technologies
desc: Netweb Technologies designs and builds high-performance computing servers, workstations, storage and AI systems under its Tyrone brand.
markets: Customers are mainly in India, including government and research bodies; international sales are limited.
rationale: Indian listed server maker with enterprise and government buyers; F1 India presence could help, but brand marketing is limited.

name: Nominal
desc: Nominal sells a platform for testing and operating hardware systems, used by defence, aerospace and robotics firms to analyse data.
markets: Customers are US defence, aerospace and robotics companies; no verified international operations.
rationale: Test and telemetry software for engineering teams; F1 data-heavy engineering offers a technology tie-in, though defence customers dominate.

name: Oasis Security
desc: Oasis Security sells software for managing non-human identities and AI agent access for enterprises.
markets: Enterprise customers in the US and Israel; wider regional footprint is not confirmed.
rationale: Enterprise cybersecurity vendor; CrowdStrike, Okta and Zscaler sponsor F1, so sector precedent and B2B hospitality value are credible.
